parsed_output.target_core_mechanism: Fixed rotating schedule with a shared calendar and limited sign‑up windows
feasibility_notes: Logical design is straightforward: a rotating order can be generated algorithmically and published on any shared calendar platform
Limited sign‑up windows can be enforced by automated reminders and lock‑out after the window closes
No complex resource allocation beyond calendar visibility is required
reality_dependencies: Access to a shared, editable calendar system that all members can view (e.g., Google Calendar, Outlook)
Reliable notification mechanism to alert members when a sign‑up window opens and closes
Agreement among members to respect the rotating order and not bypass the window
Time‑zone handling if members are distributed across regions
claims_needing_evidence: The rotating schedule will distribute in‑person spots more evenly over time compared to ad‑hoc sign‑up
Limited sign‑up windows will eliminate the advantage of rapid registration and reduce race conditions
Members will perceive the system as fair and will comply without significant resistance
potential_blockers: Technical limitations of the chosen calendar platform (API rate limits, edit conflicts)
Members forgetting or missing the sign‑up window, leading to unfilled spots
Resistance from members accustomed to first‑come‑first‑served sign‑ups
Synchronization issues for members in different time zones
candidate_tests: Run a 4‑week pilot where the schedule is applied to a real meeting series and record sign‑up timestamps for each spot
Compare the distribution of allocated spots across members before and after implementation using variance metrics
Survey participants after the pilot to assess perceived fairness and willingness to continue using the system
Measure the number of missed or unfilled spots due to window closures versus prior unrestricted sign‑up
exploratory_candidate_tests: Simulate a weighted lottery where tickets are assigned based on past attendance and compare allocation equity to the rotating schedule
Implement a points‑based credit system for contributions and test redemption rates for in‑person spots
Conduct A/B testing between the rotating schedule and a simple lottery to evaluate member satisfaction and perceived fairness
